            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Reality is closer to a continuum. <a href="https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.31887/DCNS.2003.5.2/macrocq">Alcohol, nicotine and caffeine</a> are psychoactive chemicals that can cause varying degrees of problems, but they were never lumped together with heroin. And even when cannabis was prohibited, neither sentencing guidelines nor the public equated its dangers with crack. The public was sophisticated enough to know that some drugs cause more harm.</p>

<p>Gambling also challenges black-and-white thinking. It <a href="https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1360-0443.2010.03126.x">triggers neural pathways</a> similar to those activated by drug addiction, and the <a href="https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/dsm">American Psychiatric Association’s diagnostic manual</a> recognizes that it can produce compulsive, self-destructive behavior even without a drug involved. Yet no compulsion-inducing product – not even the powerful synthetic opioid fentanyl – always induces addictive or self-destructive behavior. After all, many patients have “used” fentanyl during surgery. </p>

<p>Countries regulate gambling with that variation in mind. Until recent decades, <a href="https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF12761">the U.S. banned commercial sports betting</a>. <a href="https://www.jcrc.go.jp/en/policy/regulatory/casino.html">Japan limits casino visits</a> to a set number per week or month. Norway permits gambling <a href="https://www.regjeringen.no/en/topics/culture-sports-and-non-profit-work/lotteries-and-gaming/innsiktsartikler/gaming-in-norway/id2521199">only via state monopolies</a> aimed at preventing gambling problems and at funneling profits to nonprofits.</p>

<p>I’m not arguing that Japan’s or Norway’s gambling policies are right, or that the U.S. should follow <a href="https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/australia-social-media-ban-takes-effect-world-first-2025-12-09">Australia</a>, <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/indonesias-social-media-curbs-kids-set-saturday-few-know-how-it-will-work-2026-03-27">Indonesia</a> and <a href="https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/malaysia-bars-under-16s-signing-up-social-media-2026-06-01">Malaysia</a> in blocking youth social media accounts. I’m only suggesting such actions merit real debate, not automatic dismissal.</p>

<p>Binary distinctions between bad and good don’t work because products and their features vary widely in how likely they are to cause regrettable, repetitive engagement. Free societies rightly presume that adults can manage their own affairs without government interference – but children are a different matter, and even adult freedom has exceptions.</p>

<h2>Is TikTok engineered to addict?</h2>

<p>Pennsylvania’s lawsuit charges that TikTok is engineered to trap users and thereby maximize the time they spend generating revenue for the company. That is reminiscent of cigarette manufacturers <a href="https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK179276/">intentionally modifying chemical formulations</a>, such as <a href="https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.329.7469.757-a">adding ammonia compounds</a>, to enhance the speed and efficiency of nicotine absorption to maintain user addiction. </p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A teen boy is scrolling through videos on his phone." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=450&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=450&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=450&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=566&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=566&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757335/original/file-20260901-60-71249i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=566&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">The lawsuit states TikTok knows the app’s design causes anxiety, depression and lack of sleep but chooses profit over child safety.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/in-this-photo-illustration-two-teenagers-aged-14-years-old-news-photo/2266614093?adppopup=true">Anna Barclay/Getty Images News via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>On the other hand, keeping users continuously engaged – through casino floor design, gym membership contracts or automated billing for subscriptions – is a mainstream strategy across industries. Plenty of legal, respected organizations use it to maximize profit.</p>

<p>Likewise, reputable studies also find some degree of dopamine response to <a href="https://doi.org/10.1038/30498">video games</a>, <a href="https://doi.org/10.3390/nu15122671">milkshakes</a> and <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/nn.2726">even music</a>. The intensity of that response is far lower than what drugs such as cocaine or heroin produce, but it illustrates that one should not leap from the mere existence of a dopamine response to a reflexive ban. </p>

<p>Ideally, legislatures would strike a balance between freedom and protecting the minority who’d misuse it. But lately, state and national legislatures have been stalled by <a href="https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/kosa-privacy-social-media-senate.html">partisan division</a>, <a href="https://pluribusnews.com/news-and-events/new-social-media-regulation-proposals-are-on-tap-in-states/">swayed by commercial interests</a> and <a href="https://thehill.com/policy/technology/5853514-states-take-up-kids-online-safety-as-congress-stalls/">reluctant to pass new restrictions</a>.</p>

<h2>When courts do the regulating</h2>

<p>Given this legislative lethargy, state attorneys general sometimes step in to protect the public from companies that exploit compulsion-inducing products. Pittsburgh Public Schools made a similar case years before Sunday’s lawsuit: The district <a href="https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/pittsburgh/news/pittsburgh-public-schools-file-federal-lawsuit-against-multiple-social-media-platforms">sued TikTok and other social media platforms</a> in federal court, arguing the companies induced students to “compulsively use their services” and left the district to absorb the resulting mental health costs. That case, consolidated with <a href="https://www.business-humanrights.org/en/latest-news/usa-six-school-districts-chosen-as-bellwethers-to-go-to-trial-for-lawsuit-against-social-media-companies-for-allegedly-contributing-to-youth-mental-health-crisis/">similar suits from districts nationwide</a>, ended when TikTok settled rather than go to trial this spring – a resolution that came just months before Pennsylvania filed its own case making a similar addictive-by-design argument.</p>

<p>Important elements of modern tobacco control came not from Congress but from the <a href="https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsr031421">1998 Master Settlement Agreement</a>. This agreement resolved lawsuits brought by state attorneys general against major cigarette manufacturers. It also eliminated cigarette billboard ads, cartoon mascots like Joe Camel, most free samples and tobacco-brand sponsorships, and it banned cigarette marketing aimed at youth. Congress didn’t give the FDA <a href="https://www.fda.gov/tobacco-products/rules-regulations-and-guidance-related-tobacco-products/family-smoking-prevention-and-tobacco-control-act-overview">broad authority over tobacco</a> until a decade later, in 2009. </p>

<p>The opioid crisis provides a more recent example. <a href="https://nationalopioidsettlement.com/executive-summary">Settlements of lawsuits</a> against opioid manufacturers, distributors and pharmacy chains imposed not only <a href="https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/LSB11270">billion-dollar fines</a> but also rules governing future conduct. Johnson &amp; Johnson agreed to <a href="https://ncdoj.gov/attorney-general-josh-stein-announces-26-billion-agreement-with-opioid-distributors-manufacturer/">stop selling and promoting opioids</a> for 10 years. Major drug distributors agreed to stronger systems for identifying suspicious wholesale opioid orders and sharing distribution data, while <a href="https://www.talli.ai/blog/cvs-walgreens-walmart-opioid-settlement">CVS, Walgreens and Walmart</a> agreed to systems for flagging suspicious opioid prescriptions. Litigation accomplished some of the work ordinarily associated with regulation.</p>

<p>Regulation by litigation has drawbacks. Courts and attorneys general are no substitute for legislatures and expert regulatory agencies. But when conventional regulation fails to keep pace with powerful new products capable of inducing self-destructive, compulsive consumption, courts offer another route. </p>

<p>The path Attorney General Sunday has now opened may prove long and contentious, but the TikTok suit could come to be seen as the beginning of an important new layer of public protection against compulsion-inducing product design.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/290898/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

<title>A second hurricane just sideswiped Hawaii – why the islands’ usual force field seems to be down in 2026</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758621/original/file-20260908-50-jtmn0z.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=119%2C179%2C753%2C502&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">A satellite closeup of Hurricane Lowell on Sept. 8, 2026, after it passed just west of Kauai in the Hawaiian Islands.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://cdn.star.nesdis.noaa.gov/GOES18/ABI/SECTOR/tpw/GEOCOLOR/20262511940_GOES18-ABI-tpw-GEOCOLOR-3600x2160.jpg">NASA</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>The Hawaiian Islands <a href="https://files.hawaii.gov/dbedt/economic/databook/2022-individual/05/055422.pdf">rarely see significant hurricane damage</a>, but they just experienced the effects of their second hurricane in a year as Hurricane Lowell’s eyewall brushed Niihau, west of Kauai, on Sept. 8, 2026.</p>

<p>The hurricane brought <a href="https://weather.com/2026/09/08/storms/hurricane/hurricane-lowell-forecast-hawaii-kauai">heavy downpours, high surf and hurricane-force wind gusts</a> that pounded both islands, <a href="https://dod.hawaii.gov/hiema/hurricane-lowell-updates/">knocking out power and flooding roads</a>. Tropical storm conditions reached as far as Honolulu on the island of Oahu. </p>

<figure>
            <iframe width="440" height="260" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/oTcd22l2Oc4?wmode=transparent&amp;start=0" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>
            <figcaption><span class="caption">A video from Kauai shows the damage during Hurricane Lowell. ABC News.</span></figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Lowell was the <a href="https://www.facebook.com/TomSkilling/posts/2026-eastern-central-pacific-hurricane-season-off-to-a-running-start-a-trend-not/1708546997296903/">14th named Pacific storm</a> of 2026 and the fifth hurricane. The one that formed right after it, Hurricane Marie, sent <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/video/shorts/powerful-waves-from-hurricane-marie-slam-southern-california-269434949645">big waves to Southern California</a>, <a href="https://ktla.com/news/dana-point-homes-damaged-high-surf/">eroding coastal areas</a>, and the Pacific hurricane season doesn’t end until Nov. 30. By some metrics, the season has had the most active start since 2021.</p>

<p>In August, a near-miss by <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/cp01/cp012026.public_a.014.shtml">Hurricane Lala</a> <a href="https://www.forbes.com/sites/marshallshepherd/2026/08/15/hurricane-landfall-or-impact-what-matters-as-lala-approaches-hawaii/">brought hurricane-force winds</a> to the Hawaii’s Big Island for the first time since 1871.</p>

<p>People joke that the Hawaiian Islands have a force field keeping hurricanes away. But this year, a few things are keeping that force field down. I’m one of the few <a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=5uEy_XoAAAAJ&amp;hl=en">atmospheric scientists whose research focuses on Pacific hurricanes</a>. Here’s what I’m seeing in the eastern and central Pacific basins this year.</p>



<h2>2 reasons Hawaii is typically spared</h2>

<p>For decades, Hawaii was thought of as a special place that somehow dodged hurricanes despite its tropical location. While it lies at a similar latitude to other hurricane-prone regions, such as the Yucatan Peninsula of Mexico or the Bahamas, <a href="https://www.soest.hawaii.edu/met/Faculty/businger/poster/hurricane/">significant hurricane damage is rare</a> there.</p>

<p>Hurricanes <a href="https://www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/products/atcr/1959atcr.pdf">Dot (1959)</a>, <a href="https://dod.hawaii.gov/blog/1982-hurricane-lwa-response/">Iwa (1982)</a>, <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/CP1992_Seasonal_TCR.pdf">Iniki (1992)</a> and <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/EP142018_Lane.pdf">Lane (2018)</a> were the <a href="https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/7240">most notable storms</a> in the islands’ recorded history.</p>

<p>Iniki is often considered the worst: Its 145 mph wind gusts <a href="https://dod.hawaii.gov/blog/1992-hurricane-iniki-response/">damaged about 70% of Kauai’s homes</a> and businesses and more than 550 buildings on Oahu.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A map shows the paths of Hurricanes Iwa, Iniki, Lane and Dot across the Hawaiian Islands." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=464&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=464&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=464&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=583&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=583&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758597/original/file-20260908-70-ouxlq3.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=583&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">The paths of four notable hurricanes that directly impacted Hawaii.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><span class="source">Matthew Fibbi</span>, <a class="license" href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/4.0/">CC BY-ND</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>There are two reasons for Hawaii’s lack of more frequent hurricane impacts.</p>

<p>First, Hawaii is a pretty small target over the vast Pacific Ocean. The probability of a hurricane passing over any particular point is low, especially farther from the Mexican coast, since most Pacific hurricanes tend to stay closer to Mexico. </p>

<p>Second, the ocean itself forms a hurricane shield of sorts for the islands. The ocean has <a href="https://www.eurekalert.org/multimedia/888522">cooler water temperatures to the east</a>, where most storms approaching the islands come from. Without warm oceans to provide fuel, hurricanes tend to weaken and fizzle out as they approach the islands.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A map showing average water temperatures" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=339&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=339&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=339&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=426&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=426&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758632/original/file-20260908-50-58o8qu.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=426&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">The cooler waters to the east of Hawaii are evident in this map of average ocean temperature differences. It shows temperatures in Celsius at water depths between 20 meters and 1,000 meters (65 feet and 3,280 feet) for the two years from July 1, 2007, through June 30, 2009.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.eurekalert.org/multimedia/888522">Gerard Nihous with data from HYCOM and U.S. Navy</a>, <a class="license" href="http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Hawaii is often affected by weaker and decaying tropical systems, but their impacts are typically limited to localized flooding and large waves. That’s what Hawaii <a href="https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/hurricane-kiko-hawaii-beach-waves-rip-currents">saw from Hurricane Kiko</a> in 2025 as it weakened passing north of the islands.</p>

<p>In 2026, <a href="https://abcnews.com/US/tropical-storm-lala-forecast-impact-hawaiian-islands-weekend/story?id=135610026">Lala</a> also approached the islands from the east, but it stayed at a lower latitude, which allowed the storm to intensify over warmer-than-normal waters. Most of the storms that approach the islands from the east are forced to battle the normal “shield” of cooler ocean temperatures located to the east of the islands. </p>

<p>Lowell, like Dot, Iniki, and Lane, took a different journey this year. While all four of those storms developed to the east-southeast of the islands, they all <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/?basin=cpac&amp;season=2026&amp;utm">tracked south of the islands</a> before making a sharp turn toward the north or northwest to head toward Hawaii.</p>

<p>Dot and Iniki <a href="https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/09/04/hawaii-news/hurricane-lowells-expected-turn-resembles-paths-of-iniki-dot/">made landfall on Kauai</a>, one of the westernmost islands. Iniki was the only known landfall of a major hurricane – a Category 3 storm or higher – in the state.</p>

<p>In 2018, Hurricane Lane turned toward Oahu, but it weakened <a href="https://weather.com/storms/hurricane/news/2018-08-27-reason-for-demise-of-hurricane-lane">due to increasingly hostile atmospheric conditions</a> – including increased <a href="https://theconversation.com/what-is-wind-shear-an-atmospheric-scientist-explains-how-it-can-tear-apart-hurricanes-and-why-el-nino-ramps-it-up-213527">vertical wind shear</a>, with faster winds near the top of the storm than the bottom, making it harder for the storm to keep its organized structure – and a drier, more stable air mass. While it didn’t make landfall, Lane still brought record-breaking rainfall to the islands, with as much as 58 inches (1.47 meters) falling on the Big Island.</p>

<h2>Why Lowell made a sharp turn south of Hawaii</h2>

<p>In the eastern and central Pacific, the most <a href="https://www.atmos.albany.edu/facstaff/kristen/monsoon/eastpac.png">common tropical storm track</a> is a nearly straight line toward the west, driven by an atmospheric feature known as the <a href="https://guides.library.kapiolani.hawaii.edu/apdl/earth/high">Hawaiian High or subtropical ridge</a>. This semipermanent high-pressure system sits to the northeast of Hawaii.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A map of storm tracks in the central Pacific." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=431&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=431&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=431&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=541&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=541&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758603/original/file-20260908-50-4s994u.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=541&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">A map of tropical storms that were in the vicinity of Hawaii at some point in 2026, as of Sept. 8. Hurricane Lowell (12) made a sharp turn to the north before passing Kauai. Hurricane Lala (1) passed to the south of the islands. Storms originating in the Central Pacific and Eastern Pacific are named from separate lists, which is why 2026 had two Pacific hurricanes starting with ‘L’.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/?basin=cpac&amp;season=2026&amp;utm">NOAA</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>The Hawaiian High’s sinking air makes it harder for hurricanes to draw heat and moisture from the ocean. The result is pleasant conditions for the islands while hurricanes are steered around the edge of the high-pressure system.</p>

<p>The typical pattern around the high directs storms to the west, missing the islands. However, occasionally, low-pressure troughs can migrate southward and turn a storm toward the north, increasing its acceleration in the process, <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/ep12/ep122026.discus.032.shtml">as happened with Lowell</a>.</p>

<h2>The role of El Niño</h2>

<p>Another important player on the Pacific hurricane scene is El Niño.</p>

<p>During strong El Niño years, like 2026, the tropical Pacific is much warmer than normal. The ocean tends to be busier with hurricanes during El Niño, while the <a href="https://www.aoml.noaa.gov/how-does-el-nino-impact-atlantic-hurricane-season/">Atlantic is typically quieter</a> – as we’re seeing in 2026.</p>

<p>Researchers at the University of Hawaii-Manoa identified a <a href="https://journals.ametsoc.org/view/journals/clim/10/10/1520-0442_1997_010_2683_tcoitv_2.0.co_2.xml">significant increase in the frequency</a> and likelihood of tropical cyclones in the vicinity of Hawaii during El Niño years compared with other years. They hypothesize that El Niño years favor more Hawaiian systems due to increases in atmospheric humidity and favorable wind patterns in the region.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="A satellite view of Earth showing 3 hurricanes in a row in the Pacific" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=600&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=600&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=600&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=754&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=754&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758612/original/file-20260908-50-aefjgy.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=754&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Three hurricanes – Lowell, Karina and Marie – in the Pacific Ocean at the same time was a rare sight. Lowell reached Category 5 strength; Karina Category 4; and Marie was a tropical storm at the time the satellite image was captured on Sept. 6, 2026, but reached Category 2 strength.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/a-trio-of-tropical-cyclones-in-the-pacific/">Lauren Dauphin/NASA Earth Observatory</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>The most notable change during El Niño years is the warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures, particularly to the south and east of Hawaii. These warmer temperatures supported Lala intensifying into Category 1 hurricane as it approached the Big Island from the east and passed just south of the chain. </p>

<p>Multiple studies have also noted that <a href="https://doi.org/10.1029/2000GL011614">increases in hurricane activity</a> across the western portion of the eastern Pacific and the central Pacific generally are seen during El Niño years as well, <a href="https://doi.org/10.1002/2016GL070597">such as in 2015</a>.</p>

<h2>What’s likely for the rest of the Pacific season?</h2>

<p>Generally, as the season progresses into fall, hurricanes near Hawaii become less likely, while the risk of hurricane landfalls <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/climo/">rises for the Pacific coast of Mexico</a>.</p>

<p>In recent years, several powerful Pacific storms have made landfall in Mexico, including Hurricanes <a href="https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/EP242018_Willa.pdf">Willa (2018)</a>, <a href="https://satlib.cira.colostate.edu/event/hurricane-roslyn/">Roslyn (2022)</a> and <a href="https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/news/hurricane-otis-causes-catastrophic-damage-acapulco-mexico">Otis (2023)</a>, all of which hit during the last third of October. </p>

<p>The Atlantic, meanwhile, is forecast to remain <a href="https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/noaa-maintains-prediction-for-below-normal-atlantic-hurricane-season">much less active than normal</a>, even through the peak months of its 2026 hurricane season.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/291524/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

NASA The Hawaiian Islands rarely see significant hurricane damage , but they just experienced the effects of their second hurricane in a year as Hurricane Lowell’s eyewall brushed Niihau, west of Kauai, on Sept. 8, 2026
The hurricane brought heavy downpours, high surf and hurricane-force wind gusts that pounded both islands, knocking out power and flooding roads
Tropical storm conditions reached as far as Honolulu on the island of Oahu
A video from Kauai shows the damage during Hurricane Lowell
Lowell was the 14th named Pacific storm of 2026 and the fifth hurricane
The one that formed right after it, Hurricane Marie, sent big waves to Southern California , eroding coastal areas , and the Pacific hurricane season doesn’t end until Nov. 30
By some metrics, the season has had the most active start since 2021
In August, a near-miss by Hurricane Lala brought hurricane-force winds to the Hawaii’s Big Island for the first time since 1871
People joke that the Hawaiian Islands have a force field keeping hurricanes away
But this year, a few things are keeping that force field down
I’m one of the few atmospheric scientists whose research focuses on Pacific hurricanes

Here’s what I’m seeing in the eastern and central Pacific basins this year. 2 reasons Hawaii is typically spared For decades, Hawaii was thought of as a special place that somehow dodged hurricanes despite its tropical location
While it lies at a similar latitude to other hurricane-prone regions, such as the Yucatan Peninsula of Mexico or the Bahamas, significant hurricane damage is rare there
Hurricanes Dot (1959) , Iwa (1982) , Iniki (1992) and Lane (2018) were the most notable storms in the islands’ recorded history
Iniki is often considered the worst: Its 145 mph wind gusts damaged about 70% of Kauai’s homes and businesses and more than 550 buildings on Oahu
The paths of four notable hurricanes that directly impacted Hawaii
Matthew Fibbi , CC BY-ND There are two reasons for Hawaii’s lack of more frequent hurricane impacts
First, Hawaii is a pretty small target over the vast Pacific Ocean
The probability of a hurricane passing over any particular point is low, especially farther from the Mexican coast, since most Pacific hurricanes tend to stay closer to Mexico
Second, the ocean itself forms a hurricane shield of sorts for the islands
The ocean has cooler water temperatures to the east , where most storms approaching the islands come from
Without warm oceans to provide fuel, hurricanes tend to weaken and fizzle out as they approach the islands
The cooler waters to the east of Hawaii are evident in this map of average ocean temperature differences
It shows temperatures in Celsius at water depths between 20 meters and 1,000 meters (65 feet and 3,280 feet) for the two years from July 1, 2007, through June 30, 2009
Gerard Nihous with data from HYCOM and U.S
Navy , CC BY Hawaii is often affected by weaker and decaying tropical systems, but their impacts are typically limited to localized flooding and large waves
That’s what Hawaii saw from Hurricane Kiko in 2025 as it weakened passing north of the islands
In 2026, Lala also approached the islands from the east, but it stayed at a lower latitude, which allowed the storm to intensify over warmer-than-normal waters
Most of the storms that approach the islands from the east are forced to battle the normal “shield” of cooler ocean temperatures located to the east of the islands

<title>‘Fountain’ might make you laugh or scowl but asks important questions – a Philly art historian explains why Marcel Duchamp’s iconic 1917 sculpture still provokes</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757043/original/file-20260831-50-if4yd1.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=132%2C218%2C2674%2C1782&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">&#39;Fountain&#39; by Marcel Duchamp at the Barbican Art Gallery in London in 2013.</span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/woman-looks-at-a-piece-of-work-entitled-fountain-by-marcel-news-photo/161616665">Dan Kitwood/Getty Images</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>Marcel Duchamp’s “Fountain” <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/07/arts/design/marcel-duchamp.html">is not for everyone</a> – and it does not need to be. </p>

<p>But it does encapsulate a central concern in the philosophy of art: What makes something art, and who gets to decide? </p>

<p>Whatever our tastes, art can challenge accepted systems and make us reconsider what we think we know. </p>

<p>Duchamp’s friend and chess partner <a href="https://doi.org/10.4324/9780203427033">John Cage observed in 1988</a>, “I can’t understand why people are frightened of new ideas. I’m frightened of the old ones.” “Fountain” embodies this thinking.</p>

<p>A version of “Fountain” is part of the Philadelphia Museum of Art’s permanent collection and will appear in the museum’s <a href="https://www.philamuseum.org/exhibitions/marcel-duchamp">upcoming Duchamp retrospective</a>, which opens Oct. 10, 2026, and runs through Jan. 31, 2027. The exhibition will revisit Duchamp’s enduring questions about what art is and what it can be. </p>

<p>As an <a href="https://www.arthistorylecturer.com/">art historian</a> and former Philadelphia Museum of Art staff lecturer, I have developed an intimate knowledge of Duchamp’s art through years of teaching his work. During and after my tenure at the museum, I presented 101 lectures and led 25 gallery-based programs. Some of these focused directly on Duchamp, while others explored broader questions about originality, authorship, intention, skill and value. </p>

<p>These questions are embedded in the remarkable story of “Fountain.”</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="Black-and-white photo of man in suit behind large pane of shattered glass" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=476&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=476&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=476&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=598&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=598&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757864/original/file-20260903-50-w3p17l.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=598&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Artist Marcel Duchamp looks at his major work ‘The Bride Stripped Bare by Her Bachelors, Even (The Large Glass)’ in 1965.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/artist-marcel-duchamp-being-viewed-through-glass-of-his-news-photo/50397955">Mark Kauffman/Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<h2>Courting ‘ready-made’ controversy</h2>

<p>The 1917 original “Fountain” survives only in photographs, but 14 authorized full-scale replicas followed. The Philadelphia Museum of Art owns the earliest, signed by Duchamp in 1950.</p>

<p>“Fountain” continued a press narrative about Duchamp’s work that had begun four years earlier when his 1912 painting “<a href="https://www.philamuseum.org/objects/51449">Nude Descending a Staircase (No. 2)</a>” became a sensation at the 1913 Armory Show in New York City. Journalist Julian Street remarked that it resembled “<a href="https://blackbird-archive.vcu.edu/v12n2/gallery/street_j/cubist_page.shtml">the explosion of a shingle factory</a>.”</p>

<p>Former president Theodore Roosevelt declared that a Navajo rug in his bathroom was “<a href="https://www.sweetstudy.com/files/alaymansartexhibition-pdf">a far more satisfactory and decorative picture</a>” than the cubist artists on display at the armory.</p>

<p>By 1917, Duchamp knew that controversy could compel audiences to debate what qualified as art. With “Fountain” that debate became part of the artwork.</p>

<p>Its story began with the Society of Independent Artists exhibition in New York in April 1917. Duchamp had helped found the society and establish its democratic premise that every member could exhibit without a jury. He tested that principle by purchasing a porcelain urinal, turning it on its side, signing it “R. Mutt 1917” and submitting it under a pseudonym. </p>

<p>The organizers excluded it from the official display and placed it behind a partition outside the main exhibition area. Collector Walter Arensberg, Duchamp’s friend and fellow board member, <a href="https://books.google.com/books/about/I_Shock_Myself.html?id=Lwg4AQAAIAAJ">defended it</a> and <a href="https://archive.org/details/dialogueswithmar0000caba">reportedly intended to purchase it</a>. Both men resigned in protest.</p>

<p><a href="https://archive.artic.edu/stieglitz/">Alfred Stieglitz</a> photographed “Fountain” at his <a href="https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/267701">291 gallery</a> positioned in front of Marsden Hartley’s 1913 painting “<a href="https://unframed.lacma.org/node/1421">The Warriors</a>.” The painting depicts a German military parade, and the title of the painting suggests a battle between old and new ways of thinking. Stieglitz’s photograph appeared in the <a href="https://sdrc.lib.uiowa.edu/dada/blindman/2/images/blindman_no.2_04.pdf">May 1917 issue of The Blind Man</a>, a short-lived New York avant-garde art magazine, alongside an editorial that argued that Duchamp’s act of choosing an ordinary object created “a new thought for that object.”</p>

<figure class="align-center ">
            <img alt="Black-and-white photo of a urinal on front of dark abstract background" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=638&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=638&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=638&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=801&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=801&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757608/original/file-20260902-60-623jwo.png?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=801&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px">
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Alfred Stieglitz’s photograph of ‘Fountain’ in front of Marsden Hartley’s 1913 painting ‘The Warriors.’</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://sdrc.lib.uiowa.edu/dada/blindman/2/images/blindman_no.2_04.pdf">Alfred Stieglitz, The Blind Man No. 2, May 1917, The University of Iowa Libraries</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Duchamp called such objects “readymades,” a term historians believe he first used in a <a href="https://www.aaa.si.edu/collections/items/detail/marcel-duchamp-letter-to-suzanne-duchamp-15127">letter to his sister Suzanne</a> dated Jan. 15, 1916. His first so-called readymade was “Bicycle Wheel” (1913), which joined an inverted bicycle wheel to a wooden stool. The lost original survives through replicas, including an authorized version from 1964 that’s held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art. </p>

<p>“Bicycle Wheel” proposed that art doesn’t have to be handmade. An object can become art because the artist selects it and invites us to think about it differently.</p>

<figure class="align-center ">
            <img alt="Sculpture of bicycle wheel on a white stool in a gallery setting with people in background" src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=399&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=502&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=502&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757061/original/file-20260831-50-ynrt9i.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=502&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px">

            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<h2>Making the viewer part of the art</h2>

<p>Duchamp studied at the Académie Julian in Paris and was fully capable of traditional drawing and painting. He arrived at the readymades not because he lacked technical ability, but because he prioritized art that engaged the mind over what he called “<a href="https://pmalibrary.libraryhost.com/repositories/3/archival_objects/183807">retinal art</a>,” art that primarily pleased the eye.</p>

<p>Seeing “Fountain” in Philadelphia provides a key to two of the museum’s other great Duchamp works: “<a href="https://www.philamuseum.org/objects/54149">The Bride Stripped Bare by Her Bachelors, Even (The Large Glass)</a>” and “<a href="https://www.philamuseum.org/objects/65633">Étant donnés</a>.” The eroticism that “Fountain” implied with its associations to bodily functions evolved into frustrated desire in “The Large Glass.” In “Étant donnés,” the eroticism becomes explicit and voyeuristic, as it asks viewers to peer through holes in a weathered door.</p>

<p>Duchamp’s nod to manufactured plumbing systems in “Fountain” also anticipates his exploration of mechanical themes. In “The Large Glass,” the <a href="https://www.nortonsimon.org/art/detail/P.1963.38">nine bachelors form part of an elaborate mechanical apparatus</a>. In “Étant donnés,” an electric motor inside a cookie tin rotates a perforated disc, creating the illusion of a moving waterfall.</p>

<p>All three works shift art away from a self-contained image and toward an encounter involving object, idea, context, chance and viewer. “Fountain” transforms plumbing through the artist’s selection. “The Large Glass” incorporates chance through cracks created when it was shattered accidentally in transit – damage Duchamp repaired and embraced. “Étant donnés” incorporates found materials, including an old wooden door Duchamp obtained in Cadaqués, the Catalonian village where he and his wife, Alexina “Teeny” Duchamp, spent their summers.</p>

<p>Together, the works demonstrate that art can be a question to contemplate, a system to decipher, or an experience our actions complete. Seen together in Philadelphia, they reveal how consistently Duchamp made the viewer central to artistic meaning. </p>

            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<h2>It’s OK to laugh – or scowl</h2>

<p>Despite its philosophical seriousness, “Fountain” is deliberately absurd and comical. It is appropriate to laugh. I’ve seen viewers even get angry and irritated. Its irreverent humor, provocation and rejection of artistic convention place it within Dada, a movement that began at Zurich’s <a href="https://www.zuerich.com/en/visit/culture/cabaret-voltaire">Cabaret Voltaire</a> in 1916 as an absurdist protest against the nationalism and supposedly rational values that had led to World War I. Dada became an international movement active in Berlin, Paris and New York, and it transformed modern art.</p>

<p>The legacy of the readymades, especially “Fountain,” is difficult to overstate. They paved the way for Louise Nevelson, who transformed discarded pieces of wood into <a href="https://whitney.org/artists/941">monumental assemblages</a>, and Andy Warhol, who elevated <a href="https://www.moma.org/collection/works/79809">Campbell’s soup cans</a> into icons of American culture. Maurizio Cattelan addressed Fountain directly in 2016 with “<a href="https://www.guggenheim.org/exhibition/maurizio-cattelan-america">America</a>,” a fully functioning toilet cast in 18-karat gold. </p>

<p>Nearly a century later, Cattelan echoed Duchamp’s questions about where artistic value resides: Is it in the object, its material, its price, its context, the artist’s idea or the institution declaring it art?</p>

<p>This leads to the great paradox of Duchamp’s legacy. Art conceived to challenge permanence, originality and inherent value has itself become permanent, invaluable and iconic.</p>

<title>The Women’s Professional Baseball League is betting that women’s baseball has a future in the US</title>
    <content type="html"><figure><img src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758575/original/file-20260908-60-26o7ws.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;rect=0%2C70%2C3713%2C2475&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1050&amp;h=700&amp;fit=crop" /><figcaption><span class="caption">Ashton Lansdell of the Los Angeles Queens bats during the Women&#39;s Professional Baseball League Opening Day game against the New York Heights on Aug. 1, 2026, in Springfield, Ill. </span> <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/ashton-lansdell-of-the-los-angeles-queens-bats-during-the-news-photo/2288357986?adppopup=true">Chris Bernacchi/Diamond Images via Getty Images</a></span></figcaption></figure><p>Over 70 years after the dissolution of the <a href="https://www.aagpbl.org/history/league-history">All-American Professional Girls’ Baseball League</a> – and nearly 30 years since the end of the short-lived <a href="https://www.baseball-reference.com/bullpen/Ladies_Professional_Baseball_League">Ladies League Baseball</a> – female baseball players have been competing in a professional league of their own.</p>

<p>The Women’s Professional Baseball League began its inaugural season on Aug. 1, 2026, in front of a sellout crowd at Robin Roberts Stadium in Springfield, Illinois. Since then, the league’s four teams have battled one another across 30 games, producing highlight reel moments like <a href="https://www.mlb.com/news/kelsie-whitmore-first-three-home-run-game-in-wpbl-history">Kelsie Whitmore’s three-homer game</a> and <a href="https://x.com/wpbl_official/status/2094263561681846628">Andréanne Leblanc’s walk-off grand slam</a>.</p>



<p>The San Francisco Firebells finished the regular season <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/standings/">atop the standings</a>. The playoffs, beginning on Sept. 9, will determine the league champion.</p>

<h2>An opportune time</h2>

<p>The WPBL is appearing at a time when women’s sports in the U.S. are thriving. </p>

<p>Established leagues such as the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/may/09/wnba-growth-sustainable-franchise-valuations-valkyries">WNBA</a> and <a href="https://www.sportspro.com/analysis/womens-sport/nwsl-2026-valuations-expansion-revenue-hip-rule-trinity-rodman-marketable/">National Women’s Soccer League</a> are seeing more investment, higher team valuations, lucrative media deals and growing fanbases. Women’s sports revenue is projected to reach roughly <a href="https://www.deloitte.com/global/en/Industries/tmt/perspectives/game-changers-unlocking-potential-women-sports.html?source=athletic_moneycall_newsletter&amp;campaign=17447261&amp;userId=182218">US$3 billion</a> in 2026 – an increase of 340% in just four years. </p>

<p>The WPBL certainly hopes to capitalize on this moment. But the league is also doing something culturally significant: providing a pathway for the thousands of girls and women <a href="https://theconversation.com/women-are-reclaiming-their-place-in-baseball-252590">who choose to play baseball, not softball</a>. </p>

<p>In the U.S., women have been playing baseball since at least the 1860s. But stubborn stereotypes continue to cast baseball as a sport for men and softball as the acceptable equivalent for women. Following legal challenges, Little League Baseball <a href="https://www.littleleague.org/news/1974-the-year-little-league-changed-forever/">officially allowed girls to play</a> in 1974. However, that same year, <a href="https://www.littleleague.org/play-little-league/softball/about/">Little League Softball</a> was founded, which steered girls away from baseball and reinforced the gendered split of the two sports.   </p>

<p>Since then, there have been limited opportunities and resources available to girls and women in the U.S. who want to play baseball. Those who play Little League Baseball almost always switch to softball by high school. At the collegiate level, there are a handful of <a href="https://baseballforall.com/bfa-college-club-baseball/">women’s baseball club teams</a>, but it is not an NCAA-sanctioned sport. </p>

<p>Female ballplayers in other countries also face some of these issues. But I’ve researched and written about how <a href="https://doi.org/10.1177/0193723519884850">developmental pipelines for women’s baseball players</a> in Japan, Canada and Australia <a href="https://therisingfastball.substack.com/p/japanese-womens-baseball-is-thriving">are far more established</a> than they are in the U.S.</p>

<h2>Showcasing the world’s best players</h2>

<p>So it’s no surprise that nearly half of <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/teams-overview/">the 65 players</a> in the Women’s Professional Baseball League hail from other countries, including 11 from Canada, eight from Japan, five from Mexico and four from Australia.  </p>

<p>Japan’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/jul/31/ayami-sato-womens-professional-baseball-league-los-angeles-queens-profile">Ayami Sato</a>, picked second in the draft, is widely considered the best women’s baseball pitcher in the world. <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/thaima-maximiliana/">Thaima Maximiliana</a>, from Curacao, was a first-round draft pick for Los Angeles, and South Korea’s <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/hyeonah-kim/">Hyeonah Kim</a> signed with Boston as the fourth overall pick. </p>

<figure class="align-center ">
            <img alt="Young Asian woman wearing green catching gear stands on a baseball field." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=394&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=394&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=394&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=496&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=496&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758577/original/file-20260908-50-7y4ci3.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=496&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px">
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Hyeonah Kim of the Boston Hunters looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Queens on Aug. 26, 2026, in Springfield, Ill.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/hyeonah-kim-of-the-boston-hunters-looks-on-prior-to-the-news-photo/2292243471?adppopup=true">Alex Halloway/Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>That said, many of the American ballplayers had already made a name for themselves prior to joining the WBPL.</p>

<p><a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/kelsie-whitmore/">Kelsie Whitmore</a>, who plays for <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6579676/2025/08/28/mlb-savannah-bananas-fans-coexistence-competition/">the Savannah Bananas</a>, a traveling team known for its entertaining style of play, was the league’s first overall pick. The Bananas play <a href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/46519615/savannah-bananas-101-teams-rules-baseball-facts">Banana Ball</a>, a fast-paced variation of baseball with unconventional rules that puts spectacle and fan engagement at the heart of the game. Other women in <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana_Ball">Banana Ball</a> to sign with the WPBL include <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/denae-benites/">Denae Benites</a>, <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/valerie-perez/">Val Perez</a>, <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/ashton-lansdell/">Ashton Lansdell</a> and <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/mone-davis/">Mo’ne Davis</a>, who became the first girl to pitch a shutout at the Little League World Series in 2014. Davis actually <a href="https://www.inquirer.com/sports/mone-davis-wpbl-first-run-inaugural-game-2026-20260801.html">scored the WPBL’s first run</a>.</p>

<p>The league also features women who play for the <a href="https://www.usabaseball.com/team/womens">USA Baseball women’s national team</a>, which recently qualified for next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup.</p>

<p>Each WPBL team has a salary cap of US$95,000, <a href="https://therisingfastball.substack.com/p/wpbl-financial-realities-of-americas">so players will earn</a> roughly $6,333 for the short, eight-week season. The league is covering housing costs and living expenses for the players, and they also receive a share of the league’s sponsorship revenue, in addition to any personal endorsement deals they might secure.</p>

<h2>A nod to the past</h2>

<p>Even though the teams hail from other cities, all of the games for the inaugural season have taken place in Springfield, Illinois. </p>

<p>The location is symbolic: Springfield is where the first ticketed baseball game between two women’s teams, <a href="https://sangamoncountyhistory.org/first-ticketed-womens-baseball-game-blondes-vs-brunettes/">the Blondes and the Brunettes</a>, took place in 1875.</p>

<figure class="align-right zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="Black-and-white photo of a woman wearing a cap and a baggy uniform reading 'ALL STARS' while standing on a base and catching a ball." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=237&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=776&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=776&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=776&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=975&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=975&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/757332/original/file-20260901-60-o222nk.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=975&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>
            <figcaption>
              <span class="caption">Lizzie Murphy, known as the ‘Queen of Baseball,’ plays first base in an exhibition at Fenway Park in Boston in 1922.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/american-baseball-player-lizzie-murphy-playing-first-base-news-photo/1295193650?adppopup=true">Keystone View Company/FPG/Archive Photos/Hulton Archive via Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>In similar spirit, <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/2026/07/08/womens-pro-baseball-league-reveals-team-names-and-branding-inspired-by-trailblazing-female-pioneers/">the team names commemorate</a> trailblazing women. The New York Heights are named after <a href="https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/fw-dorothy-height/">civil rights leader Dorothy Height</a>. The Boston Hunters pay tribute to <a href="https://www.nps.gov/people/dr-harriot-kezia-hunt.htm">Harriot K. Hunt</a>, an influential medical doctor and women’s rights activist. The San Francisco Firebells honor <a href="https://www.firerescue1.com/fire-service-culture/the-history-of-coit-tower-how-a-gift-from-firebelle-lil-transformed-san-franciscos-skyline">Lillie Hitchcock Coit</a>, a philanthropist and patron of the city’s volunteer firefighters whose nickname was “Firebelle Lil.” And the Los Angeles Queens are named after Lizzie Murphy, known as the “<a href="https://sabr.org/bioproj/person/lizzie-murphy/">Queen of Baseball</a>.” Murphy was the first woman to play against Major League Baseball players when she faced Boston Red Sox players in an exhibition game at Fenway Park in 1922.</p>

<p>Meanwhile, <a href="https://www.mlb.com/news/maybelle-blair-meets-her-own-mascot-at-2026-wpbl-debut-game">the official league mascot</a> is one of the most unique in professional sports: a dancing, cartwheeling version of <a href="https://presidentlincoln.illinois.gov/oral-history/collections/blair-maybelle-1/interview-detail/">Maybelle Blair</a>, the 99-year-old former All-American Professional Girls’ Baseball League player.</p>

<h2>An uncertain future</h2>

<p>ESPN Select <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/2026/07/31/where-to-watch-the-2026-wpbl-inaugural-season/">has been broadcasting the entire season</a> for the U.S. market, with select games also being shown on the Scripps Sports Network. Fans outside of the U.S. must tune in via YouTube.</p>

<p>Even though the regular season only included 30 games, there was plenty of drama on and off the field.</p>

<p>The manager of the Boston Hunters, former MLB All-Star closer <a href="https://www.baseball-reference.com/players/f/foulkke01.shtml">Keith Foulke</a>, <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7509434/2026/08/12/wpbl-keith-foulke-fired-boston-hunters-manager/">was fired</a> just three games into the season. Three weeks later, the league faced scrutiny after a board member <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7536505/2026/08/24/wpbl-board-member-financial-concerns/">filed a civil complaint</a> alleging misuse of funds and conflicts of interest in the board’s makeup and hiring practices. </p>

<p>Yet play continued and proved exciting. San Francisco claimed the <a href="https://www.theixsports.com/features/andreanne-leblanc-grand-slam-firebells-wpbls-first-walk-off-win/">league’s first walk-off win</a> in a game that featured two grand slams. New York’s <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/players/jaida-lee/">Jaida Lee</a> emerged as a top pitcher and led the league in strikeouts and strikeout rate. Whitmore and Benites finished the season leading the league <a href="https://www.womensprobaseballleague.com/stats/">with 11 home runs apiece</a>.</p>

<figure class="align-center zoomable">
            <a aria-label="Zoomable image" href="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=1000&amp;fit=clip"><img alt="Large white-haired mascot with huge sunglasses poses with a bat next to a woman in a wheelchair also wearing the same sunglasses and posing with a bat." src="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;fit=clip" srcset="https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 600w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1200w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=600&amp;h=400&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 1800w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=45&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=1 754w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=30&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=2 1508w, https://images.theconversation.com/files/758573/original/file-20260908-50-vllyq2.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&amp;q=15&amp;auto=format&amp;w=754&amp;h=503&amp;fit=crop&amp;dpr=3 2262w" sizes="(min-width: 1466px) 754px, (max-width: 599px) 100vw, (min-width: 600px) 600px, 237px"></a>

              <span class="caption">Former All-American Girls Professional Baseball League player Maybelle Blair poses alongside the mascot she inspired prior to a game between the Boston Hunters and San Francisco Firebells on Aug. 2, 2026, in Springfield, Ill.</span>
              <span class="attribution"><a class="source" href="https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/former-all-american-girls-professional-baseball-league-news-photo/2288944104?adppopup=true">Zoe Davis/Getty Images</a></span>
            </figcaption>
          </figure>

<p>Despite the success of its inaugural season, the WPBL is ultimately a startup that faces the challenges of any new league: It needs to grow its fan base, boost its media coverage, provide quality broadcasting and remain financially solvent. </p>

<p>So what will it take for the WPBL to survive, expand and carve out its own identity in an increasingly saturated pro sports landscape?         </p>

<p>It’s worth looking to other emerging sports and leagues. <a href="https://theconversation.com/could-flag-football-one-day-leapfrog-tackle-football-in-popularity-222349">Flag football</a> is growing thanks to its inclusion as an Olympic sport and promotional and financial support from the NFL. Both Women’s Elite Rugby and the Women’s Lacrosse League hope to leverage increased interest and investment to succeed. And the <a href="https://theausl.com/about/">Athletes United Softball League</a> is utilizing its innovative rules to engage fans.</p>

<p>Questions linger about the future of the WPBL. But the league certainly has one thing in its favor: the rich history of women playing baseball, both in the U.S. and around the world.</p><img src="https://counter.theconversation.com/content/289851/count.gif" alt="The Conversation" width="1" height="1" />

body: Ashton Lansdell of the Los Angeles Queens bats during the Women's Professional Baseball League Opening Day game against the New York Heights on Aug. 1, 2026, in Springfield, Ill

Chris Bernacchi/Diamond Images via Getty Images Over 70 years after the dissolution of the All-American Professional Girls’ Baseball League – and nearly 30 years since the end of the short-lived Ladies League Baseball – female baseball players have been competing in a professional league of their own
The Women’s Professional Baseball League began its inaugural season on Aug. 1, 2026, in front of a sellout crowd at Robin Roberts Stadium in Springfield, Illinois
Since then, the league’s four teams have battled one another across 30 games, producing highlight reel moments like Kelsie Whitmore’s three-homer game and Andréanne Leblanc’s walk-off grand slam
The San Francisco Firebells finished the regular season atop the standings
The playoffs, beginning on Sept. 9, will determine the league champion
An opportune time The WPBL is appearing at a time when women’s sports in the U.S. are thriving
Established leagues such as the WNBA and National Women’s Soccer League are seeing more investment, higher team valuations, lucrative media deals and growing fanbases
Women’s sports revenue is projected to reach roughly US$3 billion in 2026 – an increase of 340% in just four years
The WPBL certainly hopes to capitalize on this moment
But the league is also doing something culturally significant: providing a pathway for the thousands of girls and women who choose to play baseball, not softball
In the U.S., women have been playing baseball since at least the 1860s
But stubborn stereotypes continue to cast baseball as a sport for men and softball as the acceptable equivalent for women
Following legal challenges, Little League Baseball officially allowed girls to play in 1974
However, that same year, Little League Softball was founded, which steered girls away from baseball and reinforced the gendered split of the two sports
Since then, there have been limited opportunities and resources available to girls and women in the U.S. who want to play baseball
Those who play Little League Baseball almost always switch to softball by high school
At the collegiate level, there are a handful of women’s baseball club teams , but it is not an NCAA-sanctioned sport
Female ballplayers in other countries also face some of these issues
But I’ve researched and written about how developmental pipelines for women’s baseball players in Japan, Canada and Australia are far more established than they are in the U.S

Showcasing the world’s best players So it’s no surprise that nearly half of the 65 players in the Women’s Professional Baseball League hail from other countries, including 11 from Canada, eight from Japan, five from Mexico and four from Australia
Japan’s Ayami Sato , picked second in the draft, is widely considered the best women’s baseball pitcher in the world
Thaima Maximiliana , from Curacao, was a first-round draft pick for Los Angeles, and South Korea’s Hyeonah Kim signed with Boston as the fourth overall pick
Hyeonah Kim of the Boston Hunters looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Queens on Aug. 26, 2026, in Springfield, Ill
Alex Halloway/Getty Images That said, many of the American ballplayers had already made a name for themselves prior to joining the WBPL
Kelsie Whitmore , who plays for the Savannah Bananas , a traveling team known for its entertaining style of play, was the league’s first overall pick
The Bananas play Banana Ball , a fast-paced variation of baseball with unconventional rules that puts spectacle and fan engagement at the heart of the game

Other women in Banana Ball to sign with the WPBL include Denae Benites , Val Perez , Ashton Lansdell and Mo’ne Davis , who became the first girl to pitch a shutout at the Little League World Series in 2014
Davis actually scored the WPBL’s first run
The league also features women who play for the USA Baseball women’s national team , which recently qualified for next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup
Each WPBL team has a salary cap of US$95,000, so players will earn roughly $6,333 for the short, eight-week season

The league is covering housing costs and living expenses for the players, and they also receive a share of the league’s sponsorship revenue, in addition to any personal endorsement deals they might secure
A nod to the past Even though the teams hail from other cities, all of the games for the inaugural season have taken place in Springfield, Illinois
